I don't always write reviews, but when I do . . . it's because the game earns it. :)
This is the first review I've written for a game and rightfully so. This game most definitely earns every ounce of positive feedback that it gets from the community. So let's get started.
(Please not that the length of each pro or con does not tell you "Oh, this con section is longer than its respective pro section so it must not be a good feature of the game". Because in all honesty, every pro outweighs every con for TL2, in my eyes.)
- COMBAT-
PRO --- Even the first Torchlight really had satisfying combat, but the overall faster movement speed and better sound design/animations, TL2 really manages to make you feel like you're just tearing through enemies! Not because it's easy, but because all of the effects, sounds, screen shakes on criticals, etc. are just fantastically designed.
CON --- While the combat is good, if you get enough enemies on screen, it can sometimes become hard to track your character (when melee) with all those pretty spell effects going off. Also, depending on your preference, hitboxes on mobs MIGHT be a problem as some have said that they are a touch too big. Luckily there is a button you can map to whatever key you want that allows you to run using that key rather than a click. This way you don't accidentally start attacking when you need to retreat!
- LOOT-
PRO --- Essentially the core of every ARPG, TL2 has lots and lots of it, but it isn't screen clutter (until end game, but that's all arpg's right? ;) Right from the get go you'll be receiving drops that you will have to think between which you would rather have. Admittedly there aren't many really, really interesting affixes for items, but the drop rate for rares is very well done. You won't find legendaries (rarest item quality) dropping everywhere either...unlike Diablo III where legendaries rain from the sky at higher levels of endgame. Even with some of the game's more advanced farming techniques I have yet to find a single legendary!! Overall, it is one of the best loot systems I've ever played with.
CON --- The only con I can think of with the loot is that on higher levels, damage mitigation (MAINLY % dmg reduction) is king. This is because the game deals with flat digits rather than percentages, so higher level mobs will quickly outscale your defenses (physical and elemental armor is nearly negligible at lvls 60-65+). There are some rare gems that give +3% or +5% reduction to all damage. So you socket your gear with A LOT of those to give you ~50% dmg reduction at higher difficulties, right? Well one of the most popular gems for this comes from farming a boss early on in the game and it doesn't drop anywhere else. This kind of limits your farming options or even defensive options since flat numbers will quickly fall short to protect you at higher levels and difficulties.
-DIFFICULTY-
PRO --- There are 4 difficulty levels - Casual, Normal, Veteran, and Elite. They are an extreme range with casual being "Build anything and faceroll everyone" to Elite being "Hey, look! A monst,ohijustdied D:". They are all available from the beginning with each difficulty able to be put in hardcore mode (die and you're dead forever). Really they are able to cater to any player's preference difficulty preference.
CON --- Well almost any player... ;) I would personally want something between normal and veteran as I find late game veteran just a touch too much for my liking (though all my characters are on vet). As soon as you go from normal to veteran, damage mitigation becomes a LOT more important for later levels. In my experience, my freedom for build options begins to be limited on veteran, but there are still a LOT of viable options for this difficulty, you just have to plan a bit more. Don't even know if this is a con, but I decided that I should put it here. :P
-GRAPHICS-
PRO --- They're a bit cartoony, colorful, wonderfully stylized, and very immersive for the world that you're in. However, colorful and cartoonish doesn't mean non-serious when it needs to be serious...Bloatfang (a boss) is a great example. So are the nether portals.
CON --- "They're a bit cartoony, colorful, and stylized." I say this because it's all personal preference. :) One ACTUAL con, albeit not a big one for the vast majority of players, is that, unless they've done it in the past several months when I have been on a break, the game is not optimized for multi-core processors. I don't know why or how or any of that, but I do know that it runs great on my laptop and I have a 2.3 GHz (3.2 w/turbo CORE technology) AMD quad core A10-4600M.
-STORY-
PRO --- I'll be honest, I'm not one for a good story in isometric ARPG's which is why this pro will personally outweigh the con for me. The pro to this game's story is that it continues character progression from the previous game and that it just fits the whole TL2 style.
CON --- Again, this isn't much a con for me since I don't involve myself in ARPG stories really, but if you like story in these types of games then it will be SOMEWHAT of a disappointent. It's definitely there and ties the game together nicely along with all the areas and bosses, but  it is nothing that is going to be award winning, that's for sure. It's just mediocre and does not add a great deal of immersion or depth to the game.
-MULTIPLAYER-
PRO --- Getting online with some friends to slay hordes up on hordes of monsters is great! The difficulty actually scales with player distance and you are not required to be in the same area at once. You can each be doing totally separate quest lines. Truthfully, farming maps with friends is the best part of multiplayer in my opinion.
CON --- If you want to climb all the NG+'s (new game plus...Goes up to Ng++++ I think) and play multiplayer there, you better know someone who will do it with you. The vast majority of people who play multiplayer are either in Ng (first playthrough) or Ng+ (second playthrough). Also, mods can potentially further separate the community. You and others have to have the same mods if you want to play together. I suggest vanilla for your first 200 or so hours though. :)
-MODS-
PRO --- There are a LOT of mods including one massive mod that may as well be an expansion (synergies mod).  People are making classes, skill rebalances, stash extenders, respec potions. It is a great community worth supporting.
CON --- As mentioned above it can separate the community in multiplayer. Once a mod is attached to a character save it "can't be removed". However, there is a tool called TL2 Rapid Respec that is REALLY handy for removing mods from character saves (along with lots of other stuff....if you're a CHEATER!! ;) so this essentially isn't a problem so long as loot on your character is not specific to a certain mod, etc.
There are more subcategories I could review like classes (which are all very fun and unique!), but I think this gives a good picture of the game so I will close out here. :)
For me it's nothing less than a 9.5 out of 10. Buy it on sale and even at full price, support the devs for their next project (whatever it is!!), and get in some great quality gaming time! :D The game is honestly worth the $60 AAA title price tag. :) We're basically stealing from them to buy it for $20 or less!!
Happy gaming!

It's a good game, I played a few stages of it, but it's pretty cool, bought it for the price, and I saw what looked like a good game of indie genre. There are times that I was nervous, others that I was happy to have passed the stage.

Friend gifted me this. Had no idea what it was going in, but was a little concerned when the "Unity for Personal Use" splash screen popped up at the start.
The first time I moved, I feel through the floor and had to press R to restart the level.
Other issues:
* I'm usually fairly lenient when it comes to art styles, but I thought this game was just really bland looking. The music was okay, but it's also MIDIs of classical music, so that's to be expected.
* The controls are mostly acceptable, but there were several instances where I would land on a platform, turn around, and jump to the next, and the actual turn felt weirdly stiff, which would throw me off and make me miss the jump. I wouldn't be surprised to find out this runs on a pre-built sample platformer engine.
* Jumping at the corner of a platform is apparently as good as landing on top of it, since you get dragged on top of it anyway.
* There are piston platforms that you're meant to jump off with the right timing so you can be launched higher into the air. I'm not usually good at that sort of thing, but it felt especially difficult to pull off here, not helped by me being launched up with seemingly random force.
* I think there's supposed to be a cutscene at the start that's broken and immediately skips itself.
* The levels feel long given the lack of checkpoints.
If you want a difficult platformer for cheap that has a "retro" aesthetic, go grab You Have to Win the Game. It's free and the art style actually makes sense. Don't spend 50 cents on this.

Clear sky introduces the faction wars, with the player being able to join a faction and conquer territory. Add to this that the game costs $10 (or $2.50, when I bought it during a sale) and this becomes a no-brainer.

Aliens vs. Predator begins with three campaigns straigh foward, a menu that could've gotten some worked done and graphics that haven't aged well to say the least, however in tends to be the atmosphere and gameplay that truly makes this game something worth playing, it represents perfectly what it tries to do in the first place, the alien campaign is a fast, dark, and greedy campaign having the most special moments all together, the predator campaign however tends to have violence, stealth, and complexity to give and share.
The marine campaign it's probrably the best campaign of any "Aliens vs Predator game" up to this date, it's scary, it's dark in quite a literal way, and most of all it's calm and flows with your own sense of immersion having a tendency to touch sore and taboo subjects that would surprise any triple aaa game developer in this day and age.
A little too dated to enjoy anymore.

It's a fun game if you have played earlier entries. For newcomers I wont recommend this game as there are no familiarities with any characters and the characters that have been introduced in this entry have little to no backstory to like them.
The music is as the past few tekkens really great, a tad too much EMD overall. Akuma is a fun character and hanndles about the same as in Street Fighter.
The story mode in this entry is this time approached differently, you will hear this reporter talk about the events that are happening and you switch mostly between hehaichi and kazuya. The game introduces 3 difficutlies at the start, if you select easy the combo's are chained easily, but the other inputs are lacking. Overal on medium the story mode is hard as the cpu keeps bashing you with cheap moves and unblockable attacks.
Other modes include a treasure mode where you can collect cosmetics, an arcade mode, vs mode and practice., Haven't touched online yet so can't say anything about the internet connection quality.
TLDR; play this game if you have played earlier entries, stray away from it if you are new to the series and maybe pick it up for 20 bucks on sale.

Overall, it's a great game, and is different from what we're used to in games.

Well.. this is a hardone. I normally start these out with something along the lines of: "If you liked X you'll like this game.", but for the life of me I can't think of a game close enough to this to liken it to.  I certainlty Can't say: "If you liked Doom or Doom 2 , you'll love this game.", because the game takes a sharp departure in aesthetics, play-style and ... AH-HA! Dead Space. If you liked Dead Space you... er, never mind. That's just it, the game feels like iot was the victim of schizophranic development. GOne now are the fast-paced, cirlcle-strafing, Shotgun-Blasting, Demon-Splattering game we remember from Doom 2. Now replaced by dark, Claustrophobic,  corridors and cheap jumpscares.
Doom3 tries to be somewhere Between Dead Space and System Shock 2 and manages to be neither.  Now credit where credit is due. The game looks gorgeous and atmospheric., when you can actuially see anything. THe Mars base actually feels like the sort of place people work and live in.  However this sort of upsets the game flow and I can't help but feel the darkness and tight corridors were there to compensate for the engine limitations, you know like the fog in Silent Hill. Unlike Silent Hill where the fog, combined with the open environment, created an an atmosphere of dread and uneasiness, DOom3's darkness is at first dread inducing  but quickly becomes just plain annoying.
The game also cheats. It has a nasty habit of spawning units just out of sight so you think you missed something. And no this isn't the normal teleport with the evil light show. Overall this game is excellent,  it has wonderful graphics,  great gameplay mechanics,  and an awe inspiring unit variety. It's almost as though they began to program the AI to be fun and tactical,  and shortly thereafter gave up and decided to give it insane advantages in order to compensate for it's strategical shortcomings.  I could go into a bit more depth but I just wanted to get this out there to notify anyone like me.
So to close this up:  This game is AMAZING if you are someone with the time, interest and talent to master RTS games well enough to play against others online.  But for me,  and people like me who enjoy struggling againt the AI because you aren't capable of hanging against other players.  I can't recomment this game as it is.

Mount and Blade's a great third/first (if you're into that latter one) hack-and-slash-or-shoot sandbox game set in the medieval ages. You can start out as a squire with a banner, a peasant that smithed stuff, a university student, or hell, even a bandit/poacher. And the best part? YOU CAN THEN GO ON AND EITHER BEAT THE CRAP OUT OF BANDITS, OR FARMERS, OR LORDS, OR KINGS, OR CARAVANS, AND THEN YOU CAN EITHER JOIN A FACTION, MAKE FRIENDS WITH LORDS/KINGS WHILE YOU BEAT THE CRAP OUT OF THE OTHER FACTIONS, OR EVEN CREATE YOUR OWN AND JUST BEAT THE CRAP OUT OF EVERYONE ELSE.
It's pretty awesome. Up to a steady 900 hours as of this review and I'm still not bored. The graphics are pretty good for the game's age and I'm looking forward to Bannerlord's release. Mount and Blade's a highly enjoyable game, especially this one (Warband). Though, don't go with those silly guns. Stick with your swords, crossbows, or if you download a mod, freaking pots of Wildfire, bombs, and pots of magic. Who needs---actually, if you find a mod with a gun that fires like an LMG, go for it. That's pretty awesome too.
Did I mention you can beat everything over and over, kill things, pillage villages, save fair maidens or take them hostage, get hitched, and create your own kingdom? Maybe. Did I mention you can tell a lord to go shove it when he insults your peasant blood or out-of-kingdom banner? You can even duel him if he gets really angry and embarrass him in front of everybody.
Oh, and you can also roll female to make the game harder, considering it's, y'know, medieval and stuff. And kick hordes of men down while you become a queen of the ages, or a lady that slices and dices more than... like... Deadpool, and stuff.
It's just a huge, massive, wide-open game full of opportunity to literally do whatever. I'd give it a shot and check it out - it's worth your intrigue.

I paid into the alpha of this open-world snowsports adventure and watched it mature.  I've been witness to the good, the bad, and the ugly.  Now, while most of those who get to play the Free to Play version of the game may want to throw thumbs down at it, I urge you to slow down and realize this.   This game is still in developtment.  Poppermost is trying new things, testing the waters to see what works and what doesn't, and using people like me, who paid in $40 to support this game, to test out a F2P model with the community for our feedback.
In the Alpha it was a great open world simulator, It's always fun to sit back and explore the landscape on summer days where snowsports aren't possible.
In the Early Game Version it was removed from the Steam Store, this was when they went over to their new launcher, started putting in the microtransactions (which are still very unpopular, mind you), and began trying to convert it into the F2P game everyone knew it would eventually become.
Today SNOW is purely a great game to relax to.  Nothing too intense, nothing too extreme, just the enjoyment of pure snowsports in a physics engine that works very well.   Multiplayer still needs some work, but Singleplayer is very enjoyable.   Everyone may want to throw their money ($59.99 currently) at Ubisoft's Steep, but I urge you to give SNOW a try.  At the modern day price of ABSOLUTELY FREE, you have nothing to lose.  Take the time to explore the mountains, get a feel for the landscape, immerse yourself in the never ending winter of SNOW.  This game is worth it, and will continue to mature and improve as time goes on, as it has since the beginning.
I recommend this game, easy 9/10 for me.  The only issue they have is the inability to earn currency other than through micropayments, which is very, VERY annoying, but not the end of the world, as you can play happily without them.

While I did enjoy this game for its lovely art style and its classic 90s era take on the adventure genre, I can only recommend this first entry in the series with some reservations.  The dystopian setting of the titular Deponia is a literal trash heap orbited by the idyllic Elysium (not to be confused with the blockbuster movie of the same name, with the same plot).  The cartooniness dulls the edge of the grim setting, but there's still some hearty meat to it.  This first entry explores much of what there is worth exploring, and the ending feels solid enough that you can easily leave it there without further sequels.
However, throughout the game the central character Rufus becomes more and more insufferable.  He's endearing at first, but near the end of the game it starts to become exhausting.  For this first entry, it's not quite a deal breaker.  But by the start of the sequel, he gets to the point of being completely intolerable.  While it's obvious they're trying to channel Guybrush Threepwood, it crosses some hard to define line at some point and he becomes so grating you just can't help but turn it off.

Deponia was something I picked up on a whim during the Steam flash sale, I've been a fan of point & clicks in the past (such as Monkey Island games) and had seen mixed reviews about Deponia; but thought at that price it was worth the risk.
I suspect Deponia is one of those games that you'll either love or absolutely hate - many reviews I saw complained about the "annoying main character", personally, I actually quite liked him and thought the dialogue was very fitting for the game.
I am extremely glad that I picked this up, the game was fun, interesting and I even liked the art style.
Deponia has manageable achievements - it's the first Steam game I've actually gotten round to getting all the achievements for. The vast majority of them you will pick up from just playing the game (provided you don't skip the puzzles) though some you may end up missing if you don't explore every possibility.
The one disappointment was that I did experience two bugs where I was unable to proceed and had to go back to earlier saves (thankfully I saved plenty of times so only had to replay 15 minutes or so of the game) and for that I am gong to take a couple of points off my final score.
Overall, Deponia provided everything I wanted from a point & click, it has a decent story and kept my attention throughout the game.
My rating: 8/10 - A good fun way to spend a few hours, in an interesting world with a lovely art style.
The game's bugs were a minor annoyance, but I found solutions to both with a quick Google.
Looking for an interesting point & click to spend a few hours on? Deponia's your game. Recommended - I'll be playing the next one very soon!

This game has quite a unique control scheme.  You control both brothers at the same time.  Big brother via left stick and trigger...Little brother via right stick and trigger.   This is the first co-op game I have played where I controlled both characters at the same time.  As simple as the controls are in layout, it is challenging at first.  The brothers must work together to navigate their world.  The story is told through body language and music.  While the characters do speak, it is not a known language (as far as I can tell).  This adds to the entire atmosphere of the game.  This story taps several different emotions as you make your way through it.  Then environments are nice and also well thought out...very creative design.  I thought this game was pretty awesome aside from the fact that it is entirely WAY to short in length.  I was left with the feeling that I wanted to play more.  I would almost agree with the 90/100 metascore if it had been a bit longer...say...3 times as long.  I purchased this game on sale for a rather inexpensive price and was not disappointed.  If you find it on sale, I would definitely recommend picking it up.  Side note...as it says in the store page...You need a controller.

The game reminded me alot of ICO with its characters speaking gibberish, and simple platforming but the world in Brothers is much more lively and light hearted.  Controling one brother with one stick and the other brother with the other stick creates some interesting gameplay.  Clever scenarios and events are always being thrown at you utilizing its unique controls. There's alot of basic puzzles here and it's all pretty easy but controling two characters at the same time to solve them makes them feel fresh and unique.
It took me 2.5 hours to beat it so Brothers is a short game but its a memorable one and should be played by all.

Extremely overrated.
The story has nice ending that's maybe very moving for somebody, but its completely undermined by the whole game before. Two brothers running around and solving ridiculously easy coop-like puzzles, that's more suitable for point&click adventures like Goblins. Locations change each other only for the sake of presenting new stunning landscape and doing nothing story-wise.
The whole game wraps it up in ~4 hours and maybe you won't be able to notice any flaws, but for me the whole experience was so boring, I was shocked, that in reality it took so little time.

On the positive side Brothers deals with a heavy story of loss. A family loses a wife and mother. The youngest son grieves the most over the loss of his mother. Now the father is ill, and the only cure is in the far reaches of the world. Two brothers set on this journey to save their dying father. A heartfelt story with a conclusion. Great gameplay design accompanies the journey. One analog stick and one trigger are assigned to each of the brothers. You must move and solve puzzles in tandem with one another. A mechanic not seen often in video games. I believe this form of control was also made not just as a tool, but to illustrate the connection these brothers share. The highest compliment I have for this game is by far the world that was created. Beautiful landscapes are around ever corner. From small villages in fall to the snow covered mountains of winter. For each amazing world is an amazing world within. Tribal sacrafices, giants at war, and creatures unseen. This was an amazing world i did not want to leave. That aside I find myself giving a negative review. For starters the game can be beat within roughly around 3 hrs at most. Short play time is always a negative factor to me regardless of how fun the journey was. In fact it matters more considering the more fun the more I want to play. The story is to be fair a story told plain and simple. No suprise ending or crazy plot twist, but no added sense of intrigue either. The game mechanic which I praise is also left unsatisfying. None of the puzzles in the game require any thought to figure out. The only hurdle to overcome is the mechanic itself, and that doesn't take long either. Sad most of all is the world. Amazing as this world is. It's left to only be a thought. No answers are given to why anything is in this world. Who are these tribesmen? Why are the giants at war? What was the unseen monster? So many wonders to see, but never any reasoning to them. I so desperately wanted this game to be an RPG. I wanted to wonder the land and explore everything the world had to offer. However, i could not. I was left with a puzzle platfomer that didn't take full advantage of this amazing world. I'm giving the game a negative review because in the end i was left...Unsatisfied. I wanted so much more from this game, and I felt like I was left with nothing. Only a couple hours passed in a very forgettable game. Which is a shame since there was so much potential.

My initial review was negative, but it was before I completed the whole game. Much as I love Doom, I simply couldn't put myself through this one. I had three attempts and everytime I got annoyed pretty quick because of technical problems with resolution (which you have to configure manually for any monitor that's not 10 years old; but once you install your game again, all the config files remain changed, but the game doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥), but for my forth try i used Doom 3 Redux mod (I strongly reccomend it - it fixes all the bugs but remains the core game untouched).
So yeah, we all know what Doom is about, so I'll skip the story part. I hardly paid any attention to it, to be frank.
Let start with positives, because yes, there are some.
- Level design (this is tricky, because this point also occures in flaws, I'll explain later) is overall good, and pretty complex
- Guns models are likeable
- The game itself is quite long
- Lockers codes, which we learn by listening personal recordings and reading e-mails of workers
- It has strong mod support, which is always welcomed
But well, these are not enough to earn the positive review. Because there are many problems I have with Doom 3. Boy, here we go:
- Almost all of the levels look exactly the same because they consist mosty of narrow corridors and cramped spaces. This is where we have to confront all these monsters, barely having the space to maneuver. Speaking of monsters,
- There is quite a lot of them, which is good, but some of them are extremely annoying (Commandos, Cherubs, most of the new-added). Another thing - after being hit (especially melee) the vision shakes as hell, and when you try to shoot immediately, you miss. This makes it barely possible to respond fire in the right direction. Find yourself surrounded by couple of melee-enemies and you lost 1/3 or 1/2 of your health in the blink of an eye. Speaking od health,
- The designers are total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s and want you to loose health. In almost every level they prepared a jumpscare, usually with monster jumping at you after you turn of open a door. You have no chance of dodging. This quickly gets infuriating and it's overused as ♥♥♥♥ - it's not four, five times - we talking at least twenty.
- There is no map - and as I said, levels can be quite complex, so you'll probably get lost once or twice
- No music! All we head is main menu theme and then some spooky-ambients. Compared to previous Doom games - a huge drawback.
- There is this infamous flashlight system, but to be frank, I don't think is that bad. You'll eventually get used to it. But since I mentioned it, I need to say the most important issue with Doom 3:
Doom 3 is not a Doom game. At least not by the standards set by two previous installments.
Doom games have setting that may look as a horror game, but they never intended to be one. And this one does. I'm not bad with it, but for the sake of convention most of the element we loved previous Dooms for - unfettered mayhem, vast areas with lots of monsters, metal-inspired soundtrack, fast-paced gameplay - are gone. What we are left with does not live to it's expectations.
Sorry, Doom 3. This review remains negative.

So I beat this game a few years ago and I am just now reviewing it, Its not like the other two DOOM games before it, ID software obviously wanted to try a more survival horror feel with this one, and I think they really captured it. Gone is the fast paced movement and destroying rooms full of demons with a shotgun and more of a slow subtle approach with jump scares and blacked out areas where you will be ambushed. There is a flashlight mechanic that you either love or hate, but I liked it from a survival horror standpoint. The game does lack the secret rooms we were all used to, id say there still is some secret rooms here and there and you have storage lockers where you need a code for goodies. but you still have hidden health packs and ammo and even data pads (which add a bit of story of the now deceased members) I honestly loved some of the data pads, some were very unnerving. Overall the game can be quite linear, there's no real way around certain areas and there can be a little back tracking to open certain doors but overall I don't think you will get lost too bad. The game is still scary and holds up pretty well today, just don't go in thinking it will be like previous DOOM entries and be prepared for a slow dark decent into Hell...

Clear Sky has it's moments. There are lots of well designed environments for geocaching. Day/night cycles highlight game's excellent shadow system. Anomaly artifacts are rare enough. Game works a lot like Shadow of Chernobyl in most aspects.
On down side, some missions aren't that much fun on harder difficulty levels, there is little or no benefits from finding hidden caches, Faction Wars seems like afterthought and won't lend much to gameplay after starting area. Looting corpses for money is very easy. But those problems aren't nothing compared how bad end game is which must be probably one of the worst I've played. It's time-constrained pipe-running in midst of one-shotting grenade-spam enemies spawning from thin air. If you eventually grind it through by memorizing enemy positions, bugged end game makes you finally turn difficulty down and restarting from auto-save. Or go to YouTube for end video.

Combat still sucks and the backpack system is extremely tedious but the game has atmosphere like no other, at least if you play with the Complete mod, a strongly recommended addition that improves graphics and adds an impressive weather system.

Tekken is back and better than ever. Tekken 7 is definitely on par with the master piece Tekken 5. With some new interesting battle sequences and "rage art" the combat feels very fluid and fresh. Every hit you take or make feels like it does and impact. The fighting is seamless and very satisfying.
Even though some of my favorite characters like Roger jr and Lei are not in the game at the time of writing this review, there is still A LOT of characters new and old to try out. The character customization has expanded and made better than ever before in a tekken game. Customization just in general has been stepped up a notch in every possible way.
So to the performance, is it playable? YES no problems at all. No crashes, bugs or unpolished content whatsoever. Tekken is here on PC for the first time and the port is flawless, more companies should follow in this example (Ubisoft).
If I were to find something to complain about then that would be the rather dull change to the arcade mode this time around. The arcade mode before used to be rather long with several enemies to fight against and individual cut scenes for every characters. Now in Tekken 7 there is only 5 battles(!) in the arcade mode and on top of that, there is no cut scenes to speak of. To be fair, there is now a chapter story to every character in the story mode itself.
The original arcade game mode from Tekken 5 is now more or less replaced by a new game mode called "treasure battle". Instead of choosing between three different opponents after every battle, it's automatic without much delay. What's also changed is there is now 2 rounds per battle instead of just 1. Lastly the ranks has been changed a little bit by name and quantity which is a welcome change.
Positives:
Great fluid gameplay
The original fighting system with great updates to it
Customization
Great main story
Story for ever character
Treasure mode
Rewarding system of earning skins/money
Flawless PC port
Negatives:
Half done arcade mode
Might be too over the top customization for some people.

Like any fighting game, there is a difficulty spike at some points, and that is to be expected. It's to make sure you are focused and enjoying yourself. The issue with that difficulty spike is at the end.
As you read earlier, I said to make sure you are in your happy place for story mode for this one reason: the final fight. I have no clue if it was designed this way or if it was on accident or if it is just simple RNG and I got the bad end. Your opponent at the end will spam the same devistating attacks that sometimes can not be blocked or just powers through your attacks. I felt as though they should have done some more testing with that final fight. Just keep that in mind when playing.

One of the best games of the late 90's and early 00's. AvP combines three unique playstyles in three full length campaigns.
The missions will take you to different locations in the AvP universe, some of them taken from the films, some brand new. The general pacing and atmosphere is somewhat unique as enemy attacks and appearances are for the large part unscripted, and can change between playthroughs, which causes a sense of suspense as each play is a bit different. The level design is solid, item pickups are strategically placed so careful resoruce management is vital for survival. The combat is usually resolved at a break-neck speed, this combined with the dark design of the levels and a meager health supply can cause panic and a genuine sense of fear.
Multiplayer is crazy fun, albeit somewhat unbalanced. While the campaigns are tailored to each race specifically the multiplayer just sort of mashes the three races together giving them some balance problems. Some weapons are too effective and essentially overpowered while some are useless completely. Fortunately weapons can be removed during the game setup eliminating some issues. Despite these objections, multiplayer is excellent in some aspects like, for example, some maps featuring destructible lighting as a tactical aid, wave style co-op mode and some interesting alternative play styles.
The marine campaign and gameplay should be familiar to all FPS players, marines are the weakest and slowest of the trio but they make up for it with bristling firepower. Marine campaign is the most atmospheric and genuinely frightening of the three, walking around dark instalations, fending off waves of drones and facehuggers evading predators and generally surviving by the skin of your teeth.
Predator campaign puts you in the shoes of a cold blooded space hunter, using a combination of melee weapons and high tech gadgets and devices to hunt your prey. Predators are the most beefy of the three able to shrug off alien claws and marine gunfire alike, however stealth and careful planning are paramount to a successful hunt. Predator campaign revolves around the hunt, from humans to exotic forms of the xenomorph.
The alien is a terrifying killing machine. It can climb walls, cover 30 meters in a single pounce, smell its prey and destroy it with a combination of razor sharp claws, barbed tail or a powerful inner jaw. Since it posseses no ranged weapons the alien must stalk it's prey (not unlike the predator), isolate it and destroy it.

Doom veterans who play this game for the first time will most likely find themselfs agrivated that it wasn't what they were expecting. "I payed for a DOOM game, not some slow crappy space shooter!" they would say. "What were they THINKING?!"
Well, here's
take on what happened:
ID team: "Alright, so we have this brand new IP we want to introduce. We're not sure yet on what it's name is, but It's going to be a dark, atmospheric, and tense first person game in the tight corridors of a space station. There will be these hideous alien creatures and parasites that turn people into zombies, and it's up to you as a staff member on the station to kill through the hordes of aliens and shut down the portal they're comming from while collecting key codes, notes, an alien artifact, and audio logs along the way."
ID execs: "Alright, the idea seems fine, but no one is going to be interested in an unknown IP. The only way we'll sign off on it is if it's part of a pre-existing series so people will actually buy.
ID team: "Well, I guess Doom takes place on Mars. Alright, I guess we can just remodel the aliens as the Doom enemies and have like, 2 hell levels thrown in and we can call it
"
So in short, yes, Doom 3 is not going to be the game you're expecting. But for what it is, it's a finely tuned Sci-Fi shooter with secrets to be found and the dark unknown to be explored. Once you're put into the right state of mind, it's a very satisfying experience.

This review is limited to the single-player campaign. There isn't much of a multiplayer community left.
I enjoyed Sniper Elite 3. The game looks great and it's fun sneaking around and sniping people. There are only 8 missions in the single-player campaign, but each map is very large and will take a while to complete. I wouldn't pay the full $50 sticker price for just 8 missions, but if you buy the game on sale it's fine. The level design is a bit uneven. Maps 1-5 are ok, 6-7 are very good, and the final map is awesome. The game also gets more fun as you go along. At first you're just dealing with rifleman, but by the final mission there are enemies wileding rocket launchers, enemies riding tanks, and enemy snipers in ghilli suits. SE3 is more limited than other war-themed shooters like Call of Duty and Battlefield. There are no vehicles to ride and every stage is set in North Africa, but with only 8 missions it doesn't overstay it's welcome.
In terms of DLC, definitely buy Saving Churchill. The Hunt for the Gray Wolf is not nearly as fun and can be skipped. Weapons packs aren't really necessary (in fact they kind of detract from the fun of earning the non-DLC weapons during the campaign, as whatever DLC weapons you buy become available immediately). But if you must, the best packs are the Axis weapons (which gives the Type 99 sniper rifle) and the Camo weapons pack (which gives a semi-automatic suppressed pistol).

I will start by saying yes I know I don't have many hours under my belt but this is more for anyone wondering how the hell do you get into such a game, especially if you arent acquaited with this style.
For my review its a game that works a fair bit different to other RTS games. This game works on Brigade to Division Level military operations, and with that comes a different way of playing. Maps are big, units are small and so for myself being a big Company of Heroes fan (which is of course company level operations) it was a bit of a step up. You find yourself in command of a lot of units, managing them to get to particular spots and out of sticky situations. For some, this is a chore and truly at first, I thought so too. There is so many unit options it can be a headache to find out what does what, variants of said item early models and late models, older outfitted units versus newer units... If i havent confused you this is the incorporation of the deck based system. It allows you to really explore how you want to play exactly. Outfit your army the way you want it. And like the rest of the game at first I hated it. I wanted things already done for me I wanted units to just fight but what you realise after playing a bit of this game, is its realistic capacity.
Infantry aren't effective against helicopters, hence you deploy anti air infantry. But anti air infantry are vunerable to armoured assaults so you deploy anti tank infantry. Or better yet, tanks. Artillery, helicopters, you name it they all have their part. Rather than most generic RTS's where specialization is somewhat important, Specialization and diversification plays a huge part in this game and that itself takes a long time to grasp. All of that just falls into tactics and operational strategy. Personally, I enjoy its flexibility but some would prefer a more linear approach.
The game looks great and you can zoom in and see all the carnage ensue on the ground. The physics can be a bit silly sometimes if you zoomed in and see tanks running into each other and reversing across fields en-masse but none the less its very impressive seeing so much going on in such a large battlespace. Naval warfare however is not something I would write home about, considering its rather basic in nature and the amount of units are not as impressive (there are also no sounds for naval ships except for guns firing!)
Sounds and music wise its okay. The music I prefer the most is from Airland Battle, Red Dragons predecessor. Sounds are pretty decent, artillery being the most exhilirating especially when zoomed in on the splash zone. Everything else sounds okay, realistic enough for it to be a tick in the box. There is almost no voice communication from your forces. it can make the game feel a little lonely at times considering they only say something when you select, move and fire. And it does not have much variety. Of course with so many units it could become rather annoying hearing so many different units under attack but as my review goes I must note this.
Overall, its a great game. Its tactically indepth to unbelievable levels. Its a challenge on all levels for strategy enthusiasts and if you like military hardware, or in game logistics system this too is your game. But I should say, its definitely not everyones game. And just because you like strategy does not mean you will enjoy this.  But give it a shot! and by shot I mean play 4 hours straight to just work it all out.
Also, if you have the game and are like "how do you make a deck how do you win" I am going to be honest, its trial and error. Try something big and broad at first. Then find out what you like to use the most. At first I liked tanks and artillery, now I like special forces raids and amphibious landings with marines. Also play with a friend, two is better than one if you dont know what youre doing.

Deponia was something I picked up on a whim during the Steam flash sale, I've been a fan of point & clicks in the past (such as Monkey Island games) and had seen mixed reviews about Deponia; but thought at that price it was worth the risk.
I suspect Deponia is one of those games that you'll either love or absolutely hate - many reviews I saw complained about the "annoying main character", personally, I actually quite liked him and thought the dialogue was very fitting for the game.
I am extremely glad that I picked this up, the game was fun, interesting and I even liked the art style.
Deponia has manageable achievements - it's the first Steam game I've actually gotten round to getting all the achievements for. The vast majority of them you will pick up from just playing the game (provided you don't skip the puzzles) though some you may end up missing if you don't explore every possibility.
The one disappointment was that I did experience two bugs where I was unable to proceed and had to go back to earlier saves (thankfully I saved plenty of times so only had to replay 15 minutes or so of the game) and for that I am gong to take a couple of points off my final score.
Overall, Deponia provided everything I wanted from a point & click, it has a decent story and kept my attention throughout the game.
My rating: 8/10 - A good fun way to spend a few hours, in an interesting world with a lovely art style.
The game's bugs were a minor annoyance, but I found solutions to both with a quick Google.
Looking for an interesting point & click to spend a few hours on? Deponia's your game. Recommended - I'll be playing the next one very soon!

A seriously entertaining point-and-click adventure game that is quite reminiscent of the Monkey Island series. Deponia features brilliant art direction, solid voice acting, and awesome soundtrack (Huzzah!). On the downside, like stated by many, the game is
short – I think it took like 5 hours in my first playthrough (apparently, this is the first installation of a trilogy, so fingers crossed for the next games). Even though the puzzles (which you can skip) are mostly fun, sometimes it gets quite tricky to find the right combination of items when you have to improvise – there were couple of instances where I gave up logic and instead tried every possible combination with the interactive objects. And when I finally figured them out, I was like “Seriously?
” But such instances were admittedly rare and definitely not the norm. On a somewhat surprising note, when I checked the texture compression option (which enables real-time compression), I started noticing a slight mouse lag and longer black screens during area transitions. Although it says that enabling that feature demands “high processing power”,  it’s funny to have a point-and-click game
on a machine that runs the likes of the Witcher 2 or Crysis 3 with high/ultra settings (then again, it could be Windows 8.1 acting up as usual). Overall, highly recommended.

Well... this is it. We've been waiting for nearly 6 years for the newest installment of TEKKEN and infinitely longer for a PC version in the franchise and it's finally here...
...and my god was it worth the wait.
This IS the defininitive version of TEKKEN. All past gallery items from every TEKKEN game ranging from TEKKEN TAG TOURNAMENT 2 back to where it all started in TEKKEN 1 are available to watch to ensure you haven't missed a thing.
The story mode is well driven and has a good flow to it all with a noticeably increasing difficulty with the enemies you fight as you progress down the line to ensure you aren't getting off too easy. Fights feel varied and the switch between mulitple characters is a great way to try most of them out and see who you enjoy playing the most.
The online so far has been flawless, matches found in seconds, connects within the same minute and fights feel tense knowing there's another person on the other end of that character you're beating to a pulp.
The offline modes boast a variety of things to do such as Arcade Battles, Survival and a new addition called Treasure Battle where in some fights, modifiers will be randomly applied to spice the matches up and give a whole new experience to the franchise.
Character customisation is bigger than it's ever been with nearly every aspect of the character's cosmetics havign the ability to be altered with endless combinations. Also added is player customisation which allows you to customise your personal HUD and the top of the screen.
As for performance, with an i7-4790k, 16GB of RAM and a GTX 1080 it's locked to a solid 60fps only using around 40% GPU usage at 1080p (meaning there's definitely room to increase the rendering scale). For people who don't know the 60fps lock is because fighting games such as TEKKEN and Mortal Kombat rely on frame data which needs to have both parties at the same frame rate to ensure they're sending and recieving the same amount of frame data.
The soundtrack is another excellent entry, keeping up with modern trends with heavy drum and bass tracks sounding like something straight off of the newest album by 'The Qemists' and other electronic songs that really drive the intensity of the fights. Other pieces however such as Mishima Building make you feel goosebumps with the mixture of strings and pounding electronic drums; sounding melodic at the same time as kick♥♥♥♥♥ Personal favourites are Dragon's Nest Final Round, Mishimia Dojo and Mishima Building.
If you actively enjoy fighting games then I cannot recommend this enough. If you've never played a fighting game then TEKKEN is a great place to start with it's countless characters and massive command list, you're sure to be able to pick it up in no time and start trying to find a main character. After all, if you don't enjoy it Steam has the refund service for a reason! My main is Bryan and has been since I first played him in TEKKEN 3.
Overall the game is definitely starting off as one of my favourite entries in the series, with my all time favoutire being TEKKEN 5, it's definitely given a run for its money. I cannot recommend this enough to fans new and old and even people who've never experienced a TEKKEN game before.
And remember...
All fights are personal

I keep coming back to this game mostly because of it's simplicity. Nothing complicated about going from match to match doing the best you can to help your team. There's one objective: to win. Doing so (and even when you lose) generates credits which ultimately help you earn more (with the purchase of better equipment and gear). Sometimes when you need a game that isn't complicated, H&G deilivers.
What this game lacks in my opinion is a stronger incentive to play as infantry. I've mentioned this on the H&G forums and some folks agree. Once you start playing H&G, you must always start as infantry. As you progress you eventually earn the right to play as other classes (like sniper, paratrooper, pilot, tank crew, etc.). You tend to find that most of the stronger infantry players are off playing other roles leaving a bunch of noobs to duke it out on the battlefield (and get wrecked by the tanks and planes).
What this does is it discourages new players and frustrates experienced players (cause the new players get wrecked and the old players have to switch back to infantry to capture the points and do whatever infantry does).
I think it is clear that new game modes need to be developed. If a Deathmatch mode existed where you are just going at it, Infantry V infantry, first one to run out of tickets loses, or same thing with tanks or planes, then the game might be a lot more interesting for new and old players. I will start by saying yes I know I don't have many hours under my belt but this is more for anyone wondering how the hell do you get into such a game, especially if you arent acquaited with this style.
For my review its a game that works a fair bit different to other RTS games. This game works on Brigade to Division Level military operations, and with that comes a different way of playing. Maps are big, units are small and so for myself being a big Company of Heroes fan (which is of course company level operations) it was a bit of a step up. You find yourself in command of a lot of units, managing them to get to particular spots and out of sticky situations. For some, this is a chore and truly at first, I thought so too. There is so many unit options it can be a headache to find out what does what, variants of said item early models and late models, older outfitted units versus newer units... If i havent confused you this is the incorporation of the deck based system. It allows you to really explore how you want to play exactly. Outfit your army the way you want it. And like the rest of the game at first I hated it. I wanted things already done for me I wanted units to just fight but what you realise after playing a bit of this game, is its realistic capacity.
Infantry aren't effective against helicopters, hence you deploy anti air infantry. But anti air infantry are vunerable to armoured assaults so you deploy anti tank infantry. Or better yet, tanks. Artillery, helicopters, you name it they all have their part. Rather than most generic RTS's where specialization is somewhat important, Specialization and diversification plays a huge part in this game and that itself takes a long time to grasp. All of that just falls into tactics and operational strategy. Personally, I enjoy its flexibility but some would prefer a more linear approach.
The game looks great and you can zoom in and see all the carnage ensue on the ground. The physics can be a bit silly sometimes if you zoomed in and see tanks running into each other and reversing across fields en-masse but none the less its very impressive seeing so much going on in such a large battlespace. Naval warfare however is not something I would write home about, considering its rather basic in nature and the amount of units are not as impressive (there are also no sounds for naval ships except for guns firing!)
Sounds and music wise its okay. The music I prefer the most is from Airland Battle, Red Dragons predecessor. Sounds are pretty decent, artillery being the most exhilirating especially when zoomed in on the splash zone. Everything else sounds okay, realistic enough for it to be a tick in the box. There is almost no voice communication from your forces. it can make the game feel a little lonely at times considering they only say something when you select, move and fire. And it does not have much variety. Of course with so many units it could become rather annoying hearing so many different units under attack but as my review goes I must note this.
Overall, its a great game. Its tactically indepth to unbelievable levels. Its a challenge on all levels for strategy enthusiasts and if you like military hardware, or in game logistics system this too is your game. But I should say, its definitely not everyones game. And just because you like strategy does not mean you will enjoy this.  But give it a shot! and by shot I mean play 4 hours straight to just work it all out.
Also, if you have the game and are like "how do you make a deck how do you win" I am going to be honest, its trial and error. Try something big and broad at first. Then find out what you like to use the most. At first I liked tanks and artillery, now I like special forces raids and amphibious landings with marines. Also play with a friend, two is better than one if you dont know what youre doing.

It’s really sad that the only fleshed out Train Simulator on PC these days is this poor excuse of a videogame.
I won’t even speak much of the thousands of dollars’ worth of DLCs - some of which are little more than a badly made 3d model being sold for a full game price. There are plenty of other reviews that cover that.
It started out fun. I enjoyed it enough to invest in some extra content (the route bundles are the least overpriced). Then I made the "mistake" of upgrading my computer.
This game, which is called Train Simulator
is almost unplayable on a 2016 computer, thanks to frequent crashes, consistently low framerates, ugly visuals, and FPS drops that are almost rhythmic with the movement and sound of the train.
I tinkered with the settings, between highest and lowest. It made no difference.
I emailed the developer. They replied after a massive delay, "but it runs perfectly on our much weaker computer!", and promptly closed the issue within days before I could get a chance to respond.
I asked the community for advice. They tried to convince me that it was most unreasonable of me to expect this 2016 release to run on my 2016 computer. Or how my set-up is "unbalanced" or "not good enough" despite running every other game flawlessly. Some referred to their real-life experience of driving trains, and how that has made their opinions on computer hardware and software paramount. But credit where its due - most of their passive-aggressive sermons began with hello and ended with thank you.
For people who have spent hundreds and thousands of dollars in this game, and are now unable to enjoy them, the dev's solution is to release a new game engine, which of course, will NOT support said hundreds and thousands worth of content. Meanwhile, they keep repackaging this broken software as a "new release" every year, and keep selling a thousand dollars more of DLCs, WITHOUT any warnings to buyers about the horrible expected performance, and without any commitment to give players their money's worth.
If you are still living in the last century, you might love this. Everyone else, (and I wish I could suggest a better alternative) wait for the new game engine next year.

RATING: 6/10
Aliens Versus Predator: Classic 2000 is exactly how it sounds. It's a reenvisioned version of the first AVP game with an enhanced engine and intuitive combat. The xenomorph and predator designs are beautiful despite the aged graphics.
THE GOOD:
The game does a stellar job of showing off the ferocity of the iconic xenomorphs. However, they don't seem as threateningly intelligent as those in the movies. Most of the time, they simply rush at you heedlessly and are little more than average cannon fodder for those weilding a pulse rifle. Combat controls are responsive and easy to handle, and a wide range of weaponry and attacks are available to each class.
THE BAD:
The bad part is the story, which truly killed it. Although the level design is good, the storyline in itself is horrendous. In fact, I didn't even know what the story was for any of the campaigns. All I know is that some fat guy on the televisions was telling me where to go and what to do, which was basically kill this, kill that, get here and complete the level. Another demoralizng part is the fact that each campaign starts and ends with a beautifully detailed CGI cutscene, but then immediatey transitions into the hideous textures of the actual game. The lack of direction as to what you should do forces players to save constantly, as you will inevitably see many cheap deaths in each campaign. Not even the extra levels beyond the main campaign are very good, as they have little to no dialogue and just give you an extra gun or a jetpack to shoot more xenomorphs. As no one ever plays the multiplayer, I can't say anything for that, and every time I try to play the other game modes, it doesn't load, which is odd considering that I have a very good computer. The part that annoyed me the most, however, was the terrible musical score, which was just annoying and nonsensical.
VERDICT:
If you're a fan of the xenomorphs or the predators, then you may enjoy this game. But if you like story, prepare for frustration, because this game has none. Graphics are hideous in comparison to other games made in this era and the enemy AI are simply stupid and kill you in cheap ways. Overall, you aren't missing anything by not playing this game.

AvP Classic, released in 1999 by Fox Interactive and developed by Rebellion, is a pinnacle of the first person shooter genre that even a decade and a half later still stands the test of time. This game marks the end of an age just prior to the new millenium console wars between Nintendo, Sony, and Microsoft. Before easter eggs and achievements and shiny objective markers guiding your way, you cursed a game as you first hugged the left wall of a level, and then right, all while furiously pressing 'e' and dodging enemies in the hopes of finding that last switch needed to progress to the next portion of the stage. What today's (dare I say 'spoiled'?) generation would call "unfair" was the standard for determining a gamer's true grit in times long past. Frustration wasn't just understandable, it was to be expected. Unfortunately times have changed, and more and more I find myself longing, and even romanticizing the memories of the new Title that caught my eye. Speaking of titles, AvP Classic is an excellent choice that tells you what you're getting. Aliens vs Predators (and yes, marines). But arguably most important, the game is a classic. Thanks to a re-release in 2000, and new age platforms such as Steam, we're able to relive these adventures on today's top of the line machines. I highly encourage anyone with a few spare bucks to give this critically acclaimed culmination the chance it deserves.

I bought this game solely for the modding and now that OpenIV was given a cease and desist letter, this seems to be the next step (and boldest so far) in anti-modding. I am outraged by this and urge anyone reading this to take a stand against this now before companies think they can get away with more of this. Companies should encourage modding, as it keeps the games alive, played, and enjoyed far beyond the amount of time that they would be vanilla. Take a look at skyrim and minecraft, just to use two examples. Anybody that has put as much time as I have into those games can vouch that they would have gotten bored with them FAR before had they not supported modding. The only reasons I can possibly think of to be against modding is in competitive games, where exploits could give one player a massive advantage over others, or in a system that relies heavily upon microtransactions. This one fits in the latter category and if anyone tells you otherwise, they are a fool. In a game that most people play for singleplayer, getting rid of mods is a terrible idea that can only possibly be justified with the shallow excuse that you then won't make as much money off of the microtransactions. Say what you will, but I say that in a full price game, microtransactions that affect anything other than cosmetics do nothing but negatively impact the community. Microtransactions belong in free to play games, or for purely cosmetic changes. They do not belong in full price games, and they CERTAINLY do not belong in games that need to sacrifice their long history of supporting great mods and enjoyable experiences just to make the company even more money. Making money should be a goal for a game company, but they should not have to sacrifice morals, gameplay, or fun to do so. This all being said, I strongly urge you to not purchase this game. If you are looking for an open world sandbox game you can have extensive fun with, I cannot recommend this game without mods. If you need an alternate game, I would recommend saints row 3 as the developers aren't trying to get rid of the vast majority of their fanbase.

Saints Row: The Third is a really fun game, in which you play the role of leader of the Saints, a rich gang which runs amok throughout the city.
There's an interesting story-line to follow, which you complete mission by mission - just about all of which involve some shooting or racing around in sporty vehicles (well, maybe some are not so sporty, but they're the exceptions).
There are also various extra missions which you can choose to take on.
Or you may even just choose to zoom around the city in your fast car, doing whatever you want - shooting at other gangs, police, military, or even innocent civilians, heaven forbid.
There is a wide selection of vehicles (cars, trucks, helicopters, planes, etc.), of which you can store a limited number to keep and use again.
You can even modify vehicles to make them hot stuff.
Some vehicles have to be unlocked by doing missions.
There's even a selection of radio stations you can play in your car (although it's a shame that, unlike the later Grand Theft Auto productions, you can't add your own MP3s to the radio).
You can also play Saints Row: The Third in a co-operative mode with a friend.
All in all, it's a game of serious shooting and major mayhem (as well as some not-so-serious shooting and minor mayhem).
However, in the name of greater social responsibility, I suggest that you use your powers only for good in the game - drive your vehicles below the designated speed limit at all times, and help little old ladies across the road - of course, you may succumb to mind-numbing boredom, but that's your lookout.
If you want a fun time, then I can highly recommend this game.

is a real-time online multiplayer car drifting game with unique "realistic" physics. The game wasn't as appealing as it was shown in the store page. It would be better if there was something where we could find help because some things are extremely complex in the game. I had no idea how to tune my car (not really an automobile expert). Everything about this game wasn't as unique as it looks. A quixotic project which failed to impress me. But I got used to it as I played on.
Although the game does metion it's "realistic" game physics, I just had trouble getting used to the controls and getting my car to move properly. I do not yet understand if the car physics were too realistic or if they were too surreal for the car to even move properly. Turns out, I was just too dumb to drive properly. There are 3 different modes in-game; Practice mode, Multiplayer and Ghost mode (Break pre-set records of other players). The game does offer Tuning options for your car but it's way too complicated for someone like me with no experience of automobiles.. Although there is a "Global chat" tab in the front page, while clicking on it though, it only shows up a list of number of players online and to view their steam profile. Multiplayer mode is working fine and there are around 20-30 players always on playing the game. Even though I am saying all the negative things about the game first, I really loved playing it and it only took me a few matches to get used to the controls and fully enjoy the game.
The graphics were not impressive. I felt that a game like this, with Ultra or High graphics, would make the game look beautiful. But that only ended up making the game a little better from Low graphics. I am not trying to say the graphics were completely bad. I'm just saying that the higher options for it could've been more better. Other than the fact that the high graphics weren't as good, the overall graphics of the game were okay.
There weren't as many bugs or glithces in game. I just had some difficulty with minor things like, if I had pressed the button to reverse my car twice, the car would automatically move backwards until other buttons have been pressed. And, I do not know if the loading screen is bugged or if it's supposed to load like that, but, the bar loads up and completes more than once, it runs like a loop which is kind of annoying and somewhat misleading. There is an to chat in-game, I guess, but I haven't been able to use it properly and my only guess would be that it is also one of those tabs found in the front page of the game.
I may have sounded a bit too harsh in my review but it is only because I have loved the game and look forward to playing it more. And to play it more, I need to enjoy it. And to enjoy it, I need you guys to fix all the things that make this game a little annoying. Good luck to you guys, you have done a great job.

So I decided to leave a review for this game because...... why not right. So I own a couple of other drifting type sims if you want to call them that. Now before anyone goes to far, this is not Need for Speed or Forza. Lets just get that out there for those who are thinking they are going to pick this up and just post top scores and go back to something else. I own a couple of other Indie based drift games if you will and my opinion is this one so far seems to be the best flushed out. The controller support works a WHOLEEEEEE lot better then in some other games of this type. Graphics are pretty good compared to others in this class as well. Its not Call of Duty but graphics are legit. Physix's are straight to a degree, nothing that wont get better with time. The tuning and modding are pretty good, nice level of tinkering but nothing to over the top. I run an all AMD setup too and dont seem to have any compatability issues either. The only real problem I have experienced worth mentioning is sometimes it will crash and go back to windows. This game is still pretty new so any other issues in game are due to this and really aren't worth talking about outside of the forums. Do i recommend this game, yes I do. It might seem like just a time waster but there is a steep learning curve to it that brings satisfaction when finally nailing it correctly to the point that you will probably spend more time playing then anticipated.
Now that was it for my review, this part is going to be more of a take it or leave it kinda segement. So for those looking for a tutorial, i can feel your pain but thats the fun sometimes. Picking up a new game and doing horrible in it untill you boss up. If you arent that type then here you go, some free advice. If you are new to this racing style, it is not about speed. Sometimes slow cruising around the track at 75 to 85 MPHs untill you get the hang of the track is the trick. There is no course map but a couple of laps should get you right. Dont go all out with mods and upgrades, like i said its not about speed. Hovering around the R2-R3 car category seems to be my sweet spot for power/control ratio. If you are using a controller I would just map out Steering, Throttle, Brake/Reverse, Handbrake, and Clutch.
Knowing how front brakes work differently from the back brakes helps too. You dont always have to rip the Ebrake when coming in, and braking isnt always going to give you better control in the turns as you exit. Sometimes quickly hitting the clutch a few times will straighten it out. Just depends on car. If you need a training wheel type understanding then do this. Only upgrade , suspension, steering, clutch, and then lighten the car up. You will be surprised. Hopefully this will help some people out, but no matter what, practice makes perfect. This is a great game and worth trying if you are a motorsports enthusiasis. lol

I'm going to be Really Honest, DOOM 3 wasn't the Best Entry in the Series for me, but its still a Pretty Good Game no matter what I Disliked about it.
Pros+
+Good Gameplay.
+Creepy Atmosphere.
+Good Level Design.
+Some of the Enemy Models are well made, they kinda look as if H.R. Gieger Designed them.
+A Sinister Villain (Dr. Betruger).
+Has Mod Support.
Cons-
-Level Design whilst Impressive is Very Linear, Narrow Coridors and Almost little to no Alternative Paths, there are some Secret Areas though like in the Original DOOM.
-A Majority of the Story Elements were Copied from Half-Life, though to be Fair Technicaly Speaking Half-Life did Copy some Story Elements from the Original DOOM & its Successor Quake.
-Some of the Weapons are Good, but some of the others are Pretty Wimpy Compared to their Counterparts in the Original DOOM, Shotgun and Chaingun for Example.
-Suspense is Ruined by Cheap Jumpscares and Cutscenes revealing the Monsters.
-Handheld Flashlight, this makes sense in a Survival Horror Game like Penumbra, but not a Game like DOOM 3 which is Focused on Action.
-The Visuals would have been Impressive for the Time DOOM 3 was Released, but to this Day its Visuals have Aged Poorly, alot of the Models and Map Textures have this Glossy Texturing that makes them look as if they were made from Plastic.
No Matter what I didn't like about this Game, I still Enjoyed it.

'Ban mods? Why, that's a great idea! It'll drive up Shark Card sales, it won't alienate that part of the playerbase who only play in singleplayer/only bought the game on PC so that they could play the game with some mods, and it certainly won't lead to a deluge of negative reviews!'
Sarcasm aside; mods were an essential part of the GTA V singleplayer experience on PC. They allowed you to do many things; use player-made weapons and vehicles, access content that's GTAO-only (especially when it comes to any update released after 'Lowriders' since that was the last update to share new content with the singleplayer mode), make it considerably easier to make movies (since you could use any character model you wanted, spawn a bunch of NPCs etc.), restore some features that hadn't been transferred over from earlier RAGE engine games (fancier Euphoria physics, shooting guns out of people's hands, physical bullet wounds...) and so on.
It was bad enough that every new update would temporarily cause a CTD if you had mods installed; now Take-Two (which should NOT be confused with Rockstar; after all, the latter company has consistently supported or at least turned a blind eye to PC modding) has more or less signalled that they don't care at all for those players who wanted to add some extra enjoyment to their singleplayer experience. Their reasoning that they took action to prevent hacking in GTAO is ridiculous considering that the targeted modding utility only affected singleplayer files and would actually prevent you from accessing GTAO if you'd installed a mod directly into the game folder instead of a separate 'mods' folder (and yes, this new folder would be ignored entirely by the game engine when playing GTAO - so it couldn't possibly affect GTAO that way either). Had I known that this would end up happening, I would have never bought GTA V on PC; in fact I don't know if I would have bought GTA V for any platform.
Had this stupidity never come to pass I'd be definitely recommending the game (or at least its singleplayer portion anyway since I care nothing for GTAO). As it is... well, that red thumbs up icon speaks for itself.

I somewhat enjoyed this game, a little, simply because it fulfills a kind of niche no other game has filled for me in quite some time, that's probably the only reason I kept playing as long as I did. however this game is also extremely frustrating as it is full of glaring balance issues and has a run away monetization system that absolutely ruins the entire game and any fun you might have had as soon as you reach the 'gold' tier of matchmaking.
Once you get into Gold Tier matchmaking all enjoyment your first ten hours gave you is going to leave instantly unless you are an extremely patient person or really enjoy this type of gameplay, you will from then on be matchmade with people with weapons twice as powerful as your own. People in tanks and planes which you have no good counter to and snipers that can one hit you with a bodyshot which is ridiculous, the rifles should do 99 damage maximum with a headshot needing to score you the one hit kill. This game isn't CoD and a rifle shouldn't one hit kill someone to the torso up to the distances that they do in this game but this is only one of the many glaring balance issues facing new players.
The base weapons when you buy them
be half as powerful as the same weapons but with upgrades leaving you at a distinct disadvantage to those who have spent more time in the game than you, or someone who has thrown money at the game. The fact a game with this much potential is being held back by what seems to be blatant greediness by the developer is a real shame. You can really feel a good game under all this somewhere but this game's monetization model absolutely and completely ruins it. If you've ever played Planetside 2 you know what to expect from this game, fork over the cash or be at a disadvantage forever. Actually the thing Planetside 2 has going over this is in Planetside 2 you don't have to pay free credits to repair your weapons, a system that absolutely goes to show just how greedy the devs are.
I'm going to give an example of what you can expect as a free player with no intention to pay money, or if you are someone without access to a means to pay for things.
I saved up to get the Mosin Nagant because I wanted to be a bolt action infantryman as semi-autos are really not to my taste, I buy it only to find it does around 50 damage a shot, thus far it has taken me about 5 hours of gameplay with a lot of matches where I have done insanely well and I still have not unlocked any of the upgrades which increase it's damage meaning I have been stuck playing at a serious disadvantage and at the rate I get the free currency even when I do unlock the upgrade, I will not be able to afford them for quite some time.
I am left using a bolt action rifle with iron sights, that does 50 damage a shot while the majority of others in the game have rifles that kill in one shot to the torso or have semi-automatic rifles that do 75 damage a shot or sub machine guns that mow you down without you having even a remote chance at fighting back.
Oh and the pistols cost a stupidly high amount of the credits so don't think you'll be having a backup sidearm any time soon.
Do not play this game unless you enjoy grinding or are willing to fork over some cash to get onto the level of everyone else.

Sniper mechanics work well enough. Playing with the aim assist on feels like cheating and playing with aim assist off is hard when you have bullet physics. Aim assist off for me and all good so far.

On a positive note the game looks good and runs great.

It's not Street Fighter V.
Tekken 7, completes the holy trinity of Tekken Games 3,5 and now 7, that refined unhealthy mechanics from their even-numbered predecessors Tekken (1,)2, 4 and 6/Tag 2. 'Bound' has been removed and replaced by 'Tailspin', a mechanic that makes attacks such as Jins neutral right kick push enemies so far away that the amount of combo continuation options are heavily reduced, as opposed to the character bouncing up from the ground right in your face, which was the case in T6 and Tag 2. It also increases the amount of space that you can gain in a single combo which is a great thing to encourage longer combos despite every consecutive attack in a combo dealing less damage. Rage Arts and Rage Drives are surprisingly non-exploitable, as well as armor moves, but they expand the game meaningfully, and make it a blast to play. Both casually, and competitively.
Not everything is gold though. The story is extremely short, its ending is an abrupt and unsatisfying cliffhanger (HL2 EP2 levels) and the battles are not very well-balanced. Either they're too easy, or they're way, WAY too hard. It is a colossal disappointment for a game that claims to be "the end of the mishima saga", which basically means that it's supposed to end the story surrounding the primary group of protagonists. Spoiler: It doesn't do that. Not at all.
Get it for the gameplay though because that's still awesome. Also support BNamco for finally bringing Tekken to PC <3

I just played an hour and a half, and let's say I have mixed feelings about the game so far.
First thing first, it runs pretty smoothly. I just have an ok config (960GTX), and the game is really well optimized. Graphics are a bit outdated for a 2017 game though, but still, Namco did a great job on this PC port.
On the gameplay side, it feels really good! Fights are extremely dynamics, reminding me of the old-school Tekken's. 36 characters, various customization items (a lot being kinda dull though) and for the rest... -Kick, punch, it's all in the mind- well it's Tekken!
On the other end, I have been EXTREMELY disapointed to notice that offline content is EXTREMELY (extremely bro!) thin! Goodbye Survival mode, Time Attack mode, or Team Battle mode ! Why the hell Namco would do that? Team Battle was so much fun to play with friends!!!
That leaves us with a classic arcade/offline mode (with barely 5 fights to get to the end), a Treasure Battle mode (an Arcade mode with treasures) an... well that's pretty much it.
I'd still recommend the game though, as it is in my opinion the best Tekken that got released these last 15 years.
But bring us back that Team Battle mode Namco !!!!
